column8: A partially eaten reindeer carcass lies in a circle of trampled, bloodstained earth. The tracks lead further.
Numerous animal tracks cover the gentle banks of the stream.
This inaccessible rock is a nesting place for numerous birds. The ground around it is covered with fish remains.
The lake is teeming with fish. Dozens of birds hunt them, swooping and diving in the water.
There are fish jumping in the waterfall, not many, but enough for a meal for the team. Perhaps we'll find more upstream.
The stream starts here - from a crystal clear mountain lake.
We've traversed the avalanche field and found no reindeer tracks on the other side. The herd might be buried at the foot of the mountain.
It seems that an avalanche came down from here not long ago. Hoof tracks disappear in the avalanche field - did the reindeer cause it?
This place eerily resembles our own camp, but destroyed by fire and riots. It seems that their generator was very nearly completed before it blew up.
It's a coal mine, but it has been evacuated after a collapse.
We followed the fugitives into the foothills, but lost the trail here - the freshly fallen snow has covered all footprints.
The dots turn out to be graves. The headstones read: Lob, Proloff and Belleau. Who they were? Why were they buried in such a remote place? We'll never know.
The tavern looks deserted. The signboard over the door says: "Pole Star - L'Étoile Polaire". The second name is in French.
As we suspected, it's just a tall rock sculpted by winds into a shape that from certain angle looks like a standing human. It's a useful landmark nonetheless.
Hundreds of huge, extremely heavy rails lie here, partially sunken into the frozen ground.
This strangely symmetrical rock formation looks like something built with human hand, but it's of completely natural origin.
The store is filled with crates used to transport steam cores - dozens of them, enough to power an entire fleet of dreadnoughts. Most of the crates are empty.
The cabin is sturdy and shielded from the prevailing winds by the rock.
The hill isn't very tall, but offers a wide view over the plain. We can see a string of dark spots not very far from here.
It's a small railway station, which look ridiculous beside the enormously wide tracks with huge rails that stretch north from here. What kind of gigantic train runs on them?
Railroad track runs from one horizon to the other. It's enormous - the rails are almost knee high and run on very wide sleepers.
An enormously huge locomotive lies on its side. It's a view both majestic and pathetic.
The big double doors of the warehouse are open. Inside there's a stack of crates full of canned food with French labels.
We found no food in the field kitchen, although it must've been used recently: there's still some water in the two large pots inside.
Here, close to the source, the stream is narrow and wild. We follow it, walking along the edge of the gorge.
Climbing the wall of snow piled high by the avalanche, we found a herd of reindeer cut off in a small valley.
Dozens of workers eye us suspiciously as we approach. They're a pitiful sight, starving and dressed in rags which don't cover their injuries.
These heavy wooden crates are used to transport valuable or fragile goods. They are stencilled with prominent signs warning against dropping them.
The drivers got out of the haulers and gathered in the circle. They seem to be troubled.
The rails are covered with ice, sometimes disappearing under it. We follow them until they are no longer visible.
There are still people here, packing their belongings and preparing dozens of coffins for transport. A young engineer approaches us.
column10: Steam Cores 1, Steam Tools 5, Wooden Materials 10

column8: The entrance to the cave is marked with trails of blood. We can hear muffled growls and roars coming from inside.
The rest of our people made camp here, too exhausted to go on. We should escort them to the city.
That's where our expedition was split up when our vehicles crashed during a snowstorm. Some of our precious supplies should be here.
The settlement seems to have been abandoned. It consists of several tidy wooden shacks that are now completely empty. An upright boulder stands at its centre.
There's not a living soul in the camp. We found about a dozen emaciated bodies. Surprisingly, most of them were amputees fitted with prostheses.
A huge ship has been dismantled here. Only its massive keel plates remain under the ice. Railroad tracks lead south.
The shelter is well supplied and built to withstand even the worst weather. An advanced steam heating system protects it from the cold.
We climbed up to the edge of the city. We stood there speechless, staring at the scene of devastation. It's a city of the dead. Most of the buildings are destroyed and the Generator has exploded.
There's nobody in the weather station, but everything still seems to be operational. We could try to find out what the scientists from Winterhome were working on.
Several pools are kept from freezing by a hot spring deep underground. Patches of hardy lichens cling to the bare rock at their edges. It looks like a good place for a hideout.
This cave is a hideout for some children who were evacuated from Winterhome. There are no adult survivors here. We should talk to the kids and take them to our city.
We're following the wide corridor of crushed ice that the American dreadnought, the USS Hephaestus, left in its wake.
This cave is or was inhabited. There are a number of footprints leading to its entrance. We should check if there's still someone alive up there.
Something's amiss at the observatory. Snow covers the precious instruments, and the dome is open, letting out a thin column of smoke. Someone's inside.
This is a convoy carrying workers that got lost in a blizzard. They are weak and have no provisions. We should listen to their story and escort them to our city.
The Coal Mine is automated. Its engine is pressurised, but the mining has stopped. The snow around it is untrodden and an eerie silence hangs in the air.
The city is modern and meticulously built. A tall tower emits a constant barrier of lightning, deflecting the incoming snow. But nobody comes out to greet us.
We climbed up to the cave. A low stone wall stands across its entrance. Behind it we can see several men.
A hot spring keeps a tiny patch of sea from freezing here. The Americans used this opportunity to set up a fishing village. It's deserted now.
Most of the machinery aboard the USS Prometheus has been dismantled and taken away. The massive steam hammer used to split the thickest ice lies broken by the ship's bow.
The door of the research station has been bashed in. There are signs of fighting inside - broken furniture, damaged scientific instruments, and spatters of blood.
Numerous snow shelters expertly built from blocks of hard-packed snow huddle around cold, burned-out campfires. A deathly silence hangs over the colony.
A brass plaque on the bridge tower reads: "Built by the people of Winterhome in AD 1887". The bridge is kept completely snow free by a working automaton!
The hole in the snow cliff leads to a small chamber. Someone lives here, but the lonely human figure we saw from afar has disappeared. It might be the sole survivor of Winterhome.
Some trees in this grove bear deep cuts in the shape of a cross. We found some bones scattered around them...
We've found the dying people Nansen's refugees told us about. They're sheltering in an ice crevasse.
As we approach the camp, we can see that its inhabitants are busy packing. They've dismantled a couple of huts to build improvised sledges.
The surface looks like it's been fractured by the shock of an underground explosion. It appears there may have been an underground base here.
This sturdy building could withstand a severe Arctic winter. It's crammed with sophisticated scientific equipment. Yet the camp seems to be abandoned.
A group of barely alive people hiding in several burrows dug into piles of snow.
The camp is built around a large hole in the ice - it might be the impact crater of a meteorite. There's a block and tackle attached to the top of the steel framework built over a hole.
The convoy's vehicles have been damaged by heavy blows. The snow is trodden and stained with what seems like buckets of blood.
It's hard to judge the crater's size from a distance. Its vastness only becomes apparent up close. The camp is empty.
The terrain drops suddenly here into a deep hollow. There are wounded people and dead bodies at its rocky bottom.
The people living in this camp are packed and ready to go. All the tents are empty. They're leaving almost nothing behind.
Numerous frozen bodies lie on the cave floor. They must have run out of fuel for their stoves.
The fence that surrounds the Arctic hut has been destroyed, shattered as if a pack of wild animals went through it.
A distinct spot in Frostland. We can use it as a waypoint for further exploration.
A distinct spot in Frostland. We can use it as a waypoint for further exploration.
The snow covering the crates is deep, but we're sure there are some valuable supplies buried down there.
The shack is falling apart, but its contents still have some value to us.
We found the wreck of some sort of vehicle. We can salvage some parts from it.
Indeed it is a sawmill. It hasn't been used in a very long time. Everything is covered in ice.
Three of the four walls are still standing, protecting a small stash of snow-covered supplies.
This used to be a large snowcat. It's steam turbine must have exploded, turning it into a heap of junk.
It's an abandoned Coal Mine. The snow around it is untrodden and an eerie silence hangs over the place.
This camp was built with very limited resources. The tents are small and ragged. They won't last long.
The "tents" in this camp are more holes than cloth, and offer almost no protection. The first snowstorm that arrives is sure to make light work of them.
The tents that form this camp are adequate, but no tent can save these people in the long run.
The forest is remarkably snow-free. We could send an outpost team here and start processing the trees for Wood.
A strange vehicle stands in the middle of the deserted village.
The black spire is composed of ancient volcanic rock. At its base, a shallow depression offers protection from the wind. A group of our people found shelter here.

The spire is composed of ancient rock of volcanic origin. At its base, a shallow depression offers protection from the wind. A group of our people found shelter here, but no one responded to our calls.
This camp belonged to the builders of the Generator. Their shacks are falling apart.
Snow has hidden every trace of the crowds that passed through here. From the shore we are unable to see the mysterious ship reported by our people. We'll have to get higher.
The majestic ocean liner rises above us as we approach the lowered gangway. Ice surrounds it from all sides.
The mast is stabilised with guy wires attached at three levels. There's a hut underneath it.
Some lords set up camp here. All of them are on the brink of death.
A series of gentle rolling hills begins here. There's a makeshift camp nestled between two of them.
A series of gentle rolling hills begins here. There's a makeshift camp nestled between two of them.
The trail is barely visible. The wind blasting through the narrow ravine between the rock faces carries the smell of campfire smoke. Our people must be close by.
Wind funnelled by the narrow ravine between the rock faces blasts us with sharp ice crystals. The trail is barely visible. It has been some time since anybody crossed the pass.
The ships we stole from the lords. Now crushed by ice and stripped of anything not firmly bolted down.
This workshop canned the fish caught in the lake. The double doors of the main entrance are wide open and the surrounding buildings have been burned down.
It's a large fishing boat. It's partially hidden under thick layers of snow.
The rockslide has revealed a sheer concrete wall with a huge, heavy steel door.
We cut the frozen body down and gently lowered it to the ground. There's a tool chest at the base of the tree.

This wreck must have been a winged flying machine - a novel design we've only heard vague rumours of. We had no idea they'd been actually been made.
There's a crack between the vault door and the frame that's wide enough to squeeze through. It's completely dark inside.
The snowcat is a wreck. It must have been going extremely fast when it hit a block of ice, perhaps in the dark or during a whiteout.
This research outpost was deserted a long time ago. It's quite old, but there might still be some useful equipment inside.
This huge machine used to haul tons of cargo until it broke. We can dismantle it to retrieve some resources.

Three of the four walls are still standing, protecting a small stash of snow-covered supplies.
This used to be a large snowcat. It's steam turbine must have exploded, turning it into a heap of junk.
Indeed, a large building stood here once. The size and number of chimneys suggest that it might have been an inn. But now their collapsed remains are all that stands among snow and ice.
We are standing in front of a ruined building whose purpose we cannot guess. It is possible that it is only a remainder of a larger complex.
It is indeed a large grotto. In the darkness filling it we find lots of animal and possibly human bones bearing teeth marks. We are in the lair of a large predator, probably a bear.
This sheltered cove was a convenient place for fishing once, until seas froze and a thick snow cap buried everything. Strong winds blew the snow away, revealing remains of fishermen's huts.

Sturdily built, Nansen's Storm Watch survived the storm and rises proudly over the snow. It was here that we have seen the last traces of the fearless polar explorer. Its walls are free of ice; someone must be inside.
A wall-like rock formation crosses our path. It almost looks like the work of human hands.
As we had hoped, we found a pass leading safely to the other side. There's also a sheltered place here where we could rest for a while.
This valley seems to have its own microclimate. It's less cold, and the waterfall, although frozen, appears to have been flowing relatively recently.
A small settlement built under the cover of rocks, in which several dozen people live. It consists of several sturdy buildings and two large greenhouses heated by hot springs.
It turns out that there is no city in the hole. Part of the ice and snow covered beach was carried away by winds of extreme force, which exposed bare rock underlying it.
Yes, Tesla City once stood here. The testament to technology, human pride and the power of nature, written in silence and stillness.
All we found are pieces of metal trapped in a thick layer of ice. It looks like some terrible force shattered a large metal structure here.
Although we've found warm springs on Frostland previously, this time we have sadly deluded ourselves.
This is definitely the former Exile Colony. It seems it has some new inhabitants.

As we get closer, it turns out that these are not rocks but huge rusted cages. There are frozen bodies inside, and some lie around the cages as well. These people were killed some time ago - their frozen bodies have been partially scavenged by animals. They lie scattered without any semblance of order or respect.

We reach the settlement built around the shipwreck. We guess that before the arrival of Frost there must have been a sea here. The settlement is populous, but its inhabitants meet us with distrust, even hostility.
Close up, it turns out that the building is not in such good condition as it seemed. The walls are partly collapsed, the dome's structure is damaged, and part of it fell inside.
This is a small goods station built at the crossroads. The routes lead north towards New London, north and east towards the mountains.
We see tents surrounded by a barbed wire fence and several people, probably guards, patrolling the area at a considerable distance from the camp.
The building, once heavily damaged, has been repaired to provide some protection against the weather. Smoke is billowing from its makeshift chimney.
The caves might be the shelter of wild animals, but it is possible that some people hid there. Anyway, we have weapons with us.

column2: 24. The Mine of the Lost Children
column8: This mine was far from depleted when we last sent people into it. Smoke is coming from its stacks - apparently people are living here.
The tall building of the meteorological station erected by Winterhome engineers did not survive the Great Storm.

The ruins of a city brought down by inept rule of a selfish and incompetent leader, and finally destroyed by the explosion of its badly operated, irreparably damaged generator. We didn't think we would ever return here.
On this bridge we came across the first automaton we saw in our lives. Now we meet here a group of workers from New London.
The shelter, designed to withstand the worst Arctic weather, has apparently failed to survive the Great Storm.
The mountain terrace slopes gently towards the valley below.
We stand at the edge of a field of ice waves stretching to the horizon.
It is indeed a ship trapped forever in the frozen sea. The broken ice around it rises in dramatic waves
A worn, crushed, rusty automaton. It looks like it has spent a long time under the ice. Perhaps the Great Storm uncovered it and that's why we were able to find it.
These must be the freshwater springs where we found a group of survivors before the Great Storm. The unfrozen part of the pond has shrunk considerably.
It's probably the grove in which we once discovered human bones buried under the trees.
We stand on the edge of a long ice crevice.
We found the rusted wreck of a snow rover.
A heavy freight trailer stuck in an ice crevice. Such vehicles used to be hauled by land dreadnoughts.
The only known city with a functional generator. Many survivors found refuge in this centre of political and economic power.

The tents in this camp are old and covered in patches. It seems to be deserted.
Some sort of machine buried under the ice. Our best guess is that it's a heavy cargo crawler.
This is some kind of temporary observation point. We'll have a better view of what's ahead of us when we get to the top of it.
This city is much bigger than ours, yet it seems far less advanced and more crowded.
One of the snow crawlers that was lost on the journey north. Disassembling it will provide us with resources.
Our supplies are covered in snow and ice. They seem undamaged, but we'll have to dig them out to be sure.
Only the top of the automaton is sticking out of the snow. Digging it out will take some effort, but should be worth it.
Our expedition's main vehicle, left hopelessly wedged in a crevasse. Exploring it will be difficult, but we have to find the Factory plans that are on board.
The air here is still - the trail ahead disappears in a milky haze. Even in the middle of the day it feels like twilight.
Steep rock faces protect us from the wind, but we fear a rockslide could happen at any moment.
A short tunnel leads into a vast natural cave complex. It seems to have been used as a warehouse. There are still some supplies here.
This mine is at risk of being buried by an avalanche at any time. It must have been abandoned a long time ago.
This building was destroyed by a powerful avalanche. Its interiors are filled with snow, but we should still be able to retrieve some resources.

Plenty of various equipment lies scattered around the trailer, probably taken out in an attempt to free it after the ice has collapsed under it.

The only dreadnought we didn't disassemble. It's stripped of supplies and in need of an overhaul, but otherwise it's intact.
The rusting remains of one of our dreadnoughts. We have stripped this machine of almost all usable materials.
The third of our dreadnoughts, wrecked by a powerful explosion. It's damaged beyond repair.
The engineers responsible for preparing the weather forecasts welcome us as we enter the building.
(non traduit)
The bridge is maintained by an automaton. Its task is to keep it free of snow in case we needed to transport resources across the ravine.
As we enter the shelter, a group of scientists and explorers greets us warmly.
There can be no doubt - this trail has been left by people. What's more, we can see a thin column of smoke on the horizon.
Near the base of the cliff, some dark forms are visible buried deep under the ice and snow.
The entrance to the cave is hidden from view and shielded from the prevailing wind.
Several pools are kept from freezing by springs gushing from the fissures in the rocky bottom. There are plenty of fish in the water.
All the trees are dead, some of them cracked from the sudden frost that must have come in the middle of the Arctic summer.
Numerous tents, empty crates, sledges... and countless frozen bodies. We're afraid we know where these poor people came from.
It's a mass grave, probably of the people who died when the third dreadnought's steam boiler exploded.
A trailer that the third dreadnought was hauling.
A vein of iron ore was exposed by a narrow crack in the ice.
